state.title: Community Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Grants
state.sum: The Washington State Department of Commerce offers grants for the purchase and installation of Level 2 and direct current fast (DC Fast) chargers for use at public, workplace, tribal, and multi-unit dwelling (MUD) locations.

state.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Grants
state.sum: The Washington State Department of Ecology offers grants for the purchase and installation of Level 2 EV chargers for use at public, fleet, workplace, and multifamily housing locations. The maximum grant award is $10,000 per plug, up to 10 plugs.

state.title: Low-Income Electric Vehicle (EV) Rebates
state.sum: The Washington EV Instant Rebate Program offers rebates to residents for the purchase or lease of a qualified new or pre-owned EV. New EVs are eligible for a rebate of up to $9,000, and pre-owned EVs are eligible for a rebate of up to $2,500.

laws.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Policies for Homeowners’ and Unit Owners’ Associations
laws.sum: A unit owners’ association, including single-family homes, apartments, and condominiums as well as planned use developments, may not prohibit or restrict the installation or use of an EV charger in a personal, noncommercial parking space.
laws.ref: Senate Bill 5129, 2025 and Revised Code of Washington 64.32.290, 64.34.395, 64.38.062, and 64.90.513

laws.title: Mandatory Electric Vehicle (EV) Charger Building Standards
laws.sum: For most non-residential occupancies, at least one parking space, or 10% of parking spaces rounded to the next whole number, must be made-ready for Level 2 EV chargers at all new buildings.
laws.ref: Revised Washington Administrative Code 19.27.540 and Washington Administrative Code 51-50-0429
